title: EU AI Act governance, transparency and human oversight
why: AI systems placed on the market or put into service under the EU AI Act must classify their risk level, disclose synthetic or AI-driven interaction to affected persons, preserve human oversight with real stop/override authority on consequential outputs, and keep traceable decision logs and technical documentation.

addRequirements.title: AI interaction and synthetic outputs are explicitly disclosed
addRequirements.statement: When a {secondary} interacts with an AI component or receives AI-generated or AI-scored content, the application shall label the output as machine-generated and expose the model identifier and purpose in both UI and API metadata.
addRequirements.definition: No person mistakes an automated output or recommendation for a human decision, and downstream systems can detect synthetic content programmatically.
addRequirements.failurePath: If model provenance metadata is missing on a generated response, the application rejects emission rather than returning unlabelled output.
acceptance: Given any AI-generated response or recommendation, when returned via API or UI, then it carries an explicit machine-generated disclosure and model version field.
Given a response missing provenance metadata, when validated at the boundary, then emission is refused.

addRequirements.title: Consequential AI decisions require human oversight and override
addRequirements.statement: When an AI output informs or triggers a consequential decision affecting a person's access, eligibility, safety or status, the application shall hold execution for an authorised human reviewer who can inspect input rationale, modify, reject or halt the system immediately.
addRequirements.definition: Human oversight is operational, not decorative: reviewers see confidence limits and inputs, can override any recommendation, and can disable automated recommendations via a stop control.
addRequirements.failurePath: If the human review queue is unavailable or the stop control is engaged, consequential actions pause or route to a manual non-AI workflow rather than auto-approving.
acceptance: Given a consequential AI recommendation, when produced, then no final state transition executes until a human reviewer records an explicit approve or override decision.
Given activation of the AI stop control, when subsequent requests arrive, then automated inference is bypassed immediately and logged.

addRequirements.title: AI runs retain traceable logs and declared risk/data documentation
addRequirements.statement: The application shall record tamper-evident execution logs for each consequential AI invocation (timestamp, model version, input reference, output summary and human reviewer identity) and ship a technical documentation record stating risk classification, intended purpose, prohibited-practice check and evaluation bounds.
addRequirements.definition: Post-market monitoring and conformity review can reconstruct how a decision was produced without storing unredacted secrets.
addRequirements.failurePath: If trace logging fails or a deployment references a model absent from the technical documentation manifest, the invocation is refused.
acceptance: Given a consequential AI run, when completed or overridden, then an immutable log entry records model version, input digest, output classification and reviewer outcome.
Given a configured model not declared in the risk and data-governance manifest, when validated, then startup or invocation fails.

addGates.statement: AI transparency labelling, human-override gating, stop-switch behaviour and traceable decision logging are proven by automated tests.
